questions.question: Compute Lerato's four adjustments and place each leftover piece on the statement of financial position.
questions.expected_answer: Depreciation: vehicle R60 000 straight-line at 15% = R9 000; equipment 20% of carrying value (20 000 − 4 000 = 16 000) = R3 200; total R12 200, no cash moving, accumulated depreciation growing by the same amounts. Accrued expense: telephone 3 300 + 300 unpaid = expense R3 600, with R300 a current liability. Prepaid expense: insurance 2 400 − 400 for next year = expense R2 000, with R400 a current asset. Accrued income: rent 8 800 + 800 outstanding = income R9 600, with R800 a current asset. Each adjustment corrects the income or expense to the true year figure and parks the difference as something owed or something owned — the matching principle.

questions.question: Build net profit and prove the statement of financial position balances.
questions.expected_answer: Trading: sales 150 000 − cost of sales 100 000 = gross profit 50 000 (checks the 50% mark-up: 100 000 × 1,5). Profit and loss: 50 000 + rent income 9 600 − expenses 39 800 (salaries 22 000, telephone 3 600, insurance 2 000, depreciation 12 200) = net profit R19 800, closed to Capital along with drawings 7 400. Position: non-current assets 90 800 (land and buildings 45 000; vehicles 60 000 − 27 000; equipment 20 000 − 7 200) plus current assets 19 200 (stock 9 500, debtors 5 200, bank 3 300, prepaid 400, accrued income 800) = 110 000; equity 88 000 + 19 800 − 7 400 = 100 400 plus current liabilities 9 600 (creditors 9 300 + accrued 300) = 110 000. The photograph balances.

questions.question: Read the gauges with comparisons, and revise the guards and the two street arithmetics.
questions.expected_answer: Gross profit on cost 50% — equals the policy, no leakage; gross profit on sales 33,3%; net profit on sales 13,2%. Current ratio 19 200/9 600 = 2:1 — comfortable; acid test 9 700/9 600 just over 1:1 — immediate debts covered without selling stock; solvency 110 000 against 9 600 — covered more than eleven times; return on equity 19 800/94 200 = 21% — several times a bank's savings rate. Guards: division of duties, numbered documents, authorisation, safeguards and independent checks, standing on the ethics of the bookkeeper and the GAAP rules. Street arithmetic: candles at prime 6 000 + overheads 1 500 = 7 500 over 500 = R15 each, R5 margin at R20; budget: receipts 11 000, payments 8 500, surplus 2 500, opening 1 500, closing R4 000, cash-only rules holding.
